Godel_Incompleteness.inherited: From Russell_Paradox: Every formal system draws a boundary — and the boundary is where the system meets what it cannot hold.
Godel_Incompleteness.question: Does a machine failing to find a proof show that no proof exists?
Godel_Incompleteness.ontology: A formal theory has axioms and inference rules; provability is relative to those rules. Truth in the intended natural numbers is a different relation. The nested-set diagram assumes soundness.
Godel_Incompleteness.experiment: Follow the machine’s loop through one attempt and its displayed verdict. Then follow a token outside the sorter’s inner PROVABLE ring and ask what evidence would justify that placement.
Godel_Incompleteness.observe: A timed arm attempts, jams and displays TRUE BUT UNPROVABLE. The sorter places predetermined tokens in nested TRUE/PROVABLE regions; it does not test formulas.
Godel_Incompleteness.limit: Incompleteness concerns sufficiently expressive, effectively axiomatized formal arithmetic under appropriate consistency assumptions. For the room’s semantic true/provable picture, state the stronger soundness assumption explicitly. Finite search failure proves no impossibility; arbitrary opinions are not thereby mathematical truths.
Godel_Incompleteness.variation: Existing: compare what the label asserts with what the moving mechanism actually establishes. Proposed: expose a small proof checker and distinguish an unchecked claim, an unsuccessful search and a metatheorem.
Godel_Incompleteness.handoff: Escher next changes the medium. Follow locally convincing connections and ask whether they can belong to one consistent spatial whole.

Do not repeat any system able to count, nor no system can prove consistency without formal qualifications. The diagram presupposes soundness, stronger than consistency. Gold-token percentage is not a measure of unprovable truths.
Try the written encounter in the actual museum, alone and with a group. Check visibility, reach, the stated response and the handoff before accepting a room baseline.
